base_properties.human_readable: Overdetermined Decline of Honor Violence: Dual-Mechanism Suppression Settlement (Composite Reading)

omegas.question: This constraint instantiates the composite_reading of kernel honor_violence_legitimacy; would instantiating drop_reading or contraction_reading instead produce a structurally different constraint?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Re-author the same standing arrangement under each sibling reading and compare computed classifications; divergence localizes the dispute to the legitimacy variable (drop vs composite) and the sufficiency variable (contraction vs composite).
omegas.impact: Under drop_reading the arrangement loses its status-expropriation victim set and computes nearer a pure coordination profile with lower epsilon; under contraction_reading it loses the coercively squeezed practitioner victim set and computes with far lower suppression. The composite's union of victim sets is what sustains the tangled_rope shape.
omegas.description: Committer structure: this file is one of three readings of the honor-violence-legitimacy kernel; sibling readings instantiate different constraints with different victim sets.

omegas.question: Was either mechanism alone sufficient anywhere — did external costs kill dueling where honor was never redefined, or did redefinition kill it where enforcement never bit?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Natural experiments across jurisdictions and periods: polities with prohibition but no honor redefinition (much of Latin America, where dueling persisted into the twentieth century despite bans), and redefinition-without-enforcement contexts; compare practice trajectories.
omegas.impact: If drop alone sufficed in any major case, the composite overweights contraction and collapses toward drop_reading's profile; if redefinition alone sufficed, it collapses toward contraction_reading. Survival of the composite requires both insufficiency findings.
omegas.description: Whether the two decline mechanisms are jointly necessary, as the composite reading asserts.

omegas.question: Did the two mechanisms operate simultaneously as independent forces, or was the honor redefinition a downstream adaptation to rising enforcement costs?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Sequence analysis of national cases: whether redefinition rhetoric predates, accompanies, or follows enforcement intensity peaks; diachronic textual analysis of honor treatises against prosecutorial records.
omegas.impact: A sequential account merges the two victim sets into one phased mechanism, changing the epsilon composition and weakening the composite's claim to be a distinct third reading rather than a periodization of one mechanism.
omegas.description: Simultaneity versus sequencing of the external-cost and redefinition mechanisms.

omegas.question: Which victim set dominates the arrangement's extractiveness — the coercively squeezed practitioners (prosecutions, courts-martial, the refusal-or-ruin squeeze) or the expropriated status holders (devaluation of martial-honor capital)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Quantify the two flows: prosecutorial severity and career destruction against measurable status-capital devaluation (marriage markets, promotion patterns, deference indicators) across the interval.
omegas.impact: Determines whether the composite's epsilon sits nearer the drop profile (coercion-dominated) or the contraction profile (expropriation-dominated), and therefore which sibling the computed classification most resembles.
omegas.description: Relative magnitude of the two mechanisms' distinct extractions.

omegas.question: Is the late-interval dormancy of the enforcement apparatus (unenforced statutes, ceremonial condemnation) decay toward an inertial remnant, or completed absorption of the function into the redefined honor norm?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Test dependence: monitor whether honor-boundary maintenance fails where enforcement is fully withdrawn; if the redefinition self-reproduces indefinitely without any enforcement input, absorption is complete.
omegas.impact: Decay supports a drift-toward-inertia reading of the arrangement's late phase; absorption supports a stable hybrid whose enforcement arm legitimately retired after the conceptual arm took the load.
omegas.description: Whether rising theater_ratio signals piton-style decay or successful function transfer.

commentary.narrative_context:
Between the Congress of Vienna and the First World War (interval unit ~= 3.3 years; t0 = 1815, t30 = 1914), the European honor classes dismantled the arrangement that had legitimated private combat. The composite reading holds that two mechanisms operated simultaneously and that each was insufficient alone: an external-cost mechanism (criminal prohibition, courts-martial, dismissal, prosecution) that raised the price of fighting while the old code still compelled it, and a conceptual-contraction mechanism (redefinition of honor as inner moral character, professionally certified respectability, press ridicule of the duel) that dissolved the compulsion itself. The two mechanisms have different victim sets: the external-cost mechanism squeezed the men still bound by the old code (junior officers trapped between regimental custom and disciplinary law; prosecuted duelists), while the contraction mechanism expropriated the traditional honor elite's status capital without touching their persons. The standing arrangement under contest — and the referent of epsilon — is this dual-mechanism suppression settlement itself, assessed by the composite reading's own lights: a genuine collective escape from the challenge-trap, carrying a real transfer of definitional authority and status space to ascending classes and the centralizing state. This file is one member of a three-story constraint family; see network.dual_formulation_note.

KEY AGENTS (by structural relationship):
- centralizing_state_bureaucracies: primary agenda-setter (institutional/arbitrage) — drafts and enforces the prohibition, collects governing authority
- traditional_honor_elite: primary payer (nominally powerful, identity_locked) — pays in status capital and legal jeopardy
- honor_bound_junior_officers: squeezed payer (moderate/trapped) — bound by the code above, punished by the law below
- rising_professional_bourgeoisie: principal beneficiary (powerful/mobile) — receives the vacated status space
- military_command_structures: dual-positioned beneficiary-payer (institutional/constrained) — gains discipline, loses officers
- anti_dueling_reformers: agenda-setting ideologue (organized/mobile) — supplies the redefinition, collects influence
- potential_duel_targets: incidental beneficiary (moderate/constrained) — receives freedom from compulsory combat
- women_of_honor_classes: excluded voice (moderate/trapped) — bears the consequences, holds no standing
- lower_class_men: excluded voice (powerless/trapped) — outside both honor economies
- historical_sociology_analyst: analytical observer (analytical/analytical) — sees the full two-mechanism structure

commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness 0.60: the settlement performed real coordination work — it walked an entire status class out of a self-enforcing trap that had been killing gentlemen over trivial slights — while simultaneously transferring definitional authority and status space away from the hereditary elite and imposing a decade-spanning squeeze on men caught between codes. Neither pure-benefit nor pure-transfer descriptions fit; the composite reading locates it squarely hybrid. Suppression 0.34 at interval end: overt enforcement decayed as the redefinition took hold, but soft sanction (ridicule, exclusion) and the deterrent shadow of dormant statutes persist. Theater_ratio 0.46: rising across the interval as the legal apparatus went progressively dormant — retained-on-the-books prohibitions, ceremonial condemnation — while the conceptual mechanism carried the actual function; it approaches but does not cross the proxy-substitution threshold, because the redefinition arm remains functionally live. Accessibility_collapse 0.58: once the redefinition is understood, the old alternative (fighting to defend honor) is closed both by law and by absurdity, but the new honor economy opened substitute channels, so collapse is substantial but incomplete. Resistance 0.62: high and durable — French dueling flourished for a century after prohibition, the German academic bout thrived under ban, prominent figures publicly defended the code, and enforcement was routinely evaded. The measurement series run on one shared seven-point grid (every tracked metric authored at every examined time point); base_extractiveness traces a rise-peak-ease arc (the mid-century squeeze on code-bound officers was the arrangement's most extractive phase; the end state extracts less overtly because compliance became voluntary), suppression_requirement traces build-up and decay of enforcement capacity, and theater_ratio rises monotonically as function migrates from tribunal to norm. The claimed_type is authored from structure (genuine coordination function plus asymmetric extraction plus active enforcement); the metrics are authored from descriptive record; neither was tuned toward the other or toward a predicted engine output.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The composite reading predicts the widest seat divergence of the three readings, because it posits two victim sets experiencing two different mechanisms. From the traditional_honor_elite seat (identity_locked), the settlement operates as expropriation: their status currency was inflated away by a redefinition they never consented to, and their honor-bound behavior was criminalized — a near-confiscatory experience. From the honor_bound_junior_officer seat (trapped), it operates as a pincer: the code above still compels, the law below now punishes — a near-coercive-capture experience. From the rising_professional_bourgeoisie and potential_duel_target seats, the same settlement operates as emancipation and coordination: the trap closes behind everyone simultaneously so no individual defection is punished by the class. The engine computes these divergent per-seat classifications from the structural data; the drop_reading would flatten the elite's grievance into a mere cost of doing business, and the contraction_reading would flatten the officers' legal peril into mere ideology — the composite insists both experiences are real and structurally distinct.
commentary.directionality_logic: The centralizing_state_bureaucracies sit nearest the beneficiary pole: they wrote the rules, prosecute under them, and collect governing authority from every successful enforcement — d near 0.0. Anti_dueling_reformers and the rising_professional_bourgeoisie likewise sit low: the former supplied the redefinition and collected influence, the latter received the vacated status space with full mobility to relocate reputation. Potential_duel_targets receive security without bearing costs — low d. Military_command_structures are genuinely dual-positioned: they benefit from a disciplined officer corps but pay in lost officers, tribunal burdens, and subordinate resentment, placing them nearer symmetric than a pure beneficiary declaration would suggest. The victim seats sit near the target pole: traditional_honor_elite bear the status expropriation with identity_locked exit (their self-concept, estates, and family history are constituted by the code — trapping pushes them toward full-target), and honor_bound_junior_officers bear the coercive squeeze with no exit at all. The excluded seats (women_of_honor_classes, lower_class_men) stand outside the derivation but mark the settlement's boundary: its benefits and burdens were both distributed strictly inside the honor classes.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem — endemic lethal private combat among the honor classes — is dead, and the enforcement arm of the settlement is visibly dormant (theater_ratio 0.46 and rising). A naive lifecycle reading calls this a zombie: statutes nobody enforces, condemnation nobody fears. The classification apparatus prevents that error in both directions. Against the zombie reading: the conceptual arm is load-bearing — the redefined honor boundary actively maintains the modern professional-respectability economy, and the disappearance verdict (world_rearranges) confirms that living arrangements depend on the settlement; the mismatch between dead founding problem and live dependency is substantive data (dead enforcement arm, live definitional arm), not noise. Against the pure-coordination reading: the settlement's history includes a half-century squeeze on code-bound officers and a permanent expropriation of the old elite's status capital, so labeling it a clean rope would erase identifiable victims. Tangled_rope holds both truths: the trap-escape was real, and the escape was purchased with someone else's coin. The mandatrophy_resolved condition is deliberately not keyed to any single metric — it is resolved by the structural finding that the arrangement outlived its founding problem precisely because its product became infrastructure.
commentary.kernel_context: Kernel: honor_violence_legitimacy — the standing arrangement by which the European honor classes legitimated private combat. This file instantiates the composite_reading: external-cost escalation (drop mechanism) and conceptual redefinition of honor (contraction mechanism) operated simultaneously, each insufficient alone. Sibling readings, authored as separate constraint files: drop_reading (the arrangement remained structurally legitimate; practice fell to external costs alone) and contraction_reading (dueling became structurally unthinkable as honor itself was redefined; external costs were not the operative cause). The composite's core premises directly contradict each sibling's core premise on a shared variable — legitimacy-contracted versus legitimacy-intact; costs-necessary-versus-insufficient versus costs-not-decisive — which is why both reading_relations are forecloses: no single historiographical framework can hold the composite's joint-necessity claim alongside either sibling's single-mechanism claim. Epsilon differs across the family by construction: drop_reading authors epsilon over a cost-imposition arrangement borne by practitioners; contraction_reading authors epsilon over a definitional-expropriation arrangement borne by the old elite; the composite authors epsilon over the union, carrying both victim sets, which is the structural delta the family exists to measure.

network.dual_formulation_note: Constraint family: the colloquial label 'why dueling died' decomposes, per the epsilon-invariance principle, into three structurally distinct claims. honor_violence_legitimacy__drop_reading (upstream component: external-cost imposition on practitioners; legitimacy treated as intact) and honor_violence_legitimacy__contraction_reading (upstream component: definitional expropriation of the old honor elite; external costs treated as inoperative) are integrated by this composite_reading, which asserts joint necessity and carries the union of victim sets. Each sibling file links back to this story via its own network.affects_constraints. The composite's epsilon (0.60) is authored over the dual-mechanism settlement and is not comparable to either sibling's epsilon without restating the referent; the family's analytical yield is precisely the divergence among the three computed classifications.

stakeholders.name: centralizing_state_bureaucracies
stakeholders.situation: Ministries of justice, war, and the interior drafted the prohibitions, directed prosecutions and courts-martial, and disciplined regiments whose officers fought. Every successful prosecution consolidated the state's claim to be the sole arbiter of legitimate force. The ministries can amend or repeal the rules at will and answer to no constituency inside the settlement.

stakeholders.name: anti_dueling_reformers
stakeholders.situation: Evangelical societies, utilitarian pamphleteers, and campaigning journalists supplied the intellectual content of the new honor: courage as moral steadiness rather than readiness to fight. They collected circulation, subscriptions, and moral authority as their critique spread, operating across borders through print and shifting attention freely.

stakeholders.name: rising_professional_bourgeoisie
stakeholders.situation: Lawyers, physicians, journalists, and industrial families whose standing rests on credentials, wealth, and respectability rather than birth and swordplay. As the old code lost definitional power, the status space it occupied opened to professional achievement; they inherit the deference the sword-aristocracy once collected, and their mobility lets them relocate reputation across cities and professions.

stakeholders.name: military_command_structures
stakeholders.situation: General staffs and regimental command wanted officers alive, obedient, and available. They ran the courts-martial and permission regimes, and in several armies regulated rather than banned the practice, attaching administrative conditions to sanctioned combats. They gain a disciplined corps but lose officers to both the field of honor and the tribunal, and they absorb the resentment of prosecuted subordinates.

stakeholders.name: traditional_honor_elite
stakeholders.situation: Hereditary officers, courtiers, and gentry whose rank and marriage prospects rest on the sword-honor code. A refused challenge means social death in their own circle; an accepted challenge now means prosecution, dismissal, or ruin as enforcement tightens. Their status capital — the deference attached to martial honor — loses market value as the definition of honor moves, and leaving the code means abandoning the identity their upbringing, estate, and family history are built on.

stakeholders.name: honor_bound_junior_officers
stakeholders.situation: Subalterns and junior officials bound from above by regimental custom that compels them to answer insults and from below by disciplinary law that punishes them for answering. Refusal ends their careers through ostracism; acceptance risks court-martial. They control neither the code that binds them nor the tribunal that judges them.

stakeholders.name: potential_duel_targets
stakeholders.situation: Younger sons, studious or eccentric officers, satirical writers — the men statistically likeliest to receive challenges. As the code's grip loosens they gain what they never chose to risk: freedom from being compelled onto the ground. Their protection arrives whether or not they ever engaged with the honor economy.

stakeholders.name: women_of_honor_classes
stakeholders.situation: Wives, mothers, and daughters of the dueling classes. They absorb the consequences — widowhood, orphaned children, households mortgaged for a dead man's point of honor — while holding no standing in either the old code, which fought over their names, or the new proceedings, which try the fighters. Nothing in the settlement consults them.

stakeholders.name: lower_class_men
stakeholders.situation: Laborers, rank-and-file soldiers, and tradesmen who suffer the same insults as their betters with none of the remedies. The old code reserved the duel for gentlemen; the new respectability economy admits them chiefly as objects of charity or discipline. The settlement's boundary lines pass above their heads.

stakeholders.name: historical_sociology_analyst
stakeholders.situation: Traces the settlement across the long arc of violence monopolization and status-order change, comparing national trajectories — British extinction by the 1850s, French persistence to 1914, German ritualization in the academic fencing bout — against the two-mechanism account. Holds no position inside the arrangement.

six_questions.coordination_function: Escaped a genuine collective-action trap: the honor code made each gentleman's refusal of a challenge ruinous to him alone while the whole class paid in blood, so no individual could defect safely. Simultaneous external-cost escalation and honor-redefinition let the class exit at once — the law raised the price of fighting while the redefinition dissolved the compulsion — instead of one defection at a time.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves definitional authority over honor from the hereditary martial elite to professional and state institutions; moves status space to the ascending bourgeoisie; moves coercive costs onto officers and gentlemen who still held the old code; moves security from compulsory combat to every man inside the redefined honor boundary.
six_questions.absent_voices: Women of the honor classes — widowed or ruined by duels — had no voice in either the code or its abolition; lower-class men, insulted as often as their betters, had entry to neither the duel nor full membership in the new respectability economy; the dueling dead speak only through coroners' registers and other people's records. The unanimity of the settlement's beneficiaries partly reflects that these seats were never in the room.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If the settlement vanished overnight — statutes repealed, redefinition unwound, old code reinstated — the challenge-trap logic would reassert among status-anxious elites, as it did historically whenever enforcement lapsed (the great dueling revival of 1815-1830). Military discipline structures, the state's violence monopoly, and the professional-respectability honor economy all rest on the displacement having held; they would rearrange around a revived private-combat regime.
six_questions.founding_problem: Endemic lethal private combat within the officer and gentleman classes: a self-enforcing honor equilibrium producing thousands of deaths and maimings, destabilizing military discipline, and denying the centralizing state its claim to monopolize legitimate force.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Corroborated from outside the beneficiary set: contemporaneous coroners' registers and military casualty returns compiled for budgetary and administrative rather than ideological reasons; ecclesiastical authorities who condemned the duel on independent doctrinal grounds and left their own records; and twentieth-century historiography (Kiernan on the duel's social history, Frevert on German honor, Nye on French dueling) written by scholars with no stake in the settlement's maintenance. No party inside the settlement's beneficiary set is relied upon for the founding problem's existence or its death.
